user.title: Connect to your Proxmox cluster
user.description: Any node will do: the cluster answers from every node. Nothing needs to be prepared on Proxmox beforehand.

data_description.verify_ssl: Leave off for Proxmox's self-signed certificate

password.title: Let Cluster Guard set itself up on {host}
password.description: Enter Proxmox's root password once. Cluster Guard uses it to create its own user `homeassistant@pve`, a role with only the rights it needs (read the cluster, protect and move VMs), and an API token. The password is not stored.

token.title: Use an existing API token
token.description: From Proxmox: Datacenter > Permissions > API Tokens. The token's user needs at least the PVEAuditor role; add VM.Migrate, VM.Replicate and Sys.Console for the Fix and Migrate actions.

data_description.token_id: In the form user@realm!tokenname, for example homeassistant@pve!cluster_guard

ha_vm.title: Which VM is Home Assistant?
ha_vm.description: Cluster {cluster} is reachable. Pick the VM this Home Assistant runs in, so Cluster Guard can watch its copies and where it runs. The likely one is pre-selected.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the node. Check the address and that port 8006 is open.
error.invalid_auth: Proxmox rejected the sign-in. Check the user and password (or token), and that the account may create users.
error.provision_failed: Signed in, but Cluster Guard could not create its user and token on Proxmox; see the Home Assistant log.
error.token_format: The token ID looks like user@realm!tokenname.
error.unknown: Unexpected answer from Proxmox; see the log.

abort.already_configured: This cluster is already set up.

options.token: I already have an API token

data_description.stale_minutes: Replication runs every minute on the recommended setup; 10 means ten missed runs before a warning.

node_down.title: Cluster node {node} is down
node_down.description:
Node **{node}** stopped responding. {online} of {total} nodes are up, so Home Assistant keeps running, but there is one less place for it to go if another node fails.

Check the node's power and network cable, then its screen. If it is dead for good: reinstall Proxmox on a replacement from the USB stick and rejoin it to the cluster (see the build plan). This message clears itself when the node is back.

degraded.title: Only {online} of {total} cluster nodes are up
degraded.description: Two or more nodes are down. If one more fails, the cluster loses its majority and Home Assistant stops on purpose. Fix the dead nodes before anything else.

quorum_lost.title: The cluster has lost quorum
quorum_lost.description: The nodes can no longer agree on who is in charge. Home Assistant may stop at any moment. Check the cluster switch and the nodes' network cables first; a switch outage looks exactly like this.

replication_stale.title: Copies of your VMs are not being made

ha_resource_error.title: Failover for {resource} is in state {state}
ha_resource_error.description: Proxmox's high-availability manager reports **{resource}** on {node} in state **{state}**. It is not being protected right now. In Proxmox, open Datacenter > HA, read the error, fix the cause (usually a node or storage problem), then set the resource's state back to started.

cluster_unreachable.title: Cluster Guard cannot reach Proxmox
cluster_unreachable.description:
No node has answered the API for several checks (last tried {host}): {error}

If Home Assistant itself is fine, the nodes may be unreachable from it: check the network between them. This message clears itself when a node answers.

ha_vm_not_protected.title: The Home Assistant VM is not fully protected

confirm.title: Protect the Home Assistant VM
confirm.description:
**{vm}** is Home Assistant. Failover resource: {ha}. Copies missing on: {missing}. Without both, a node failure takes Home Assistant down for good instead of two minutes.

Cluster Guard will make it a high-availability resource (state started, one restart, one relocation) and add a one-minute replication job to every node that has no copy yet. Nothing else is changed. Continue?

abort.no_permission: Proxmox refused: the token Cluster Guard uses may not change HA resources or replication. In Proxmox, give its user the VM.Replicate and Sys.Console privileges, or set Cluster Guard up again with the root password so it creates its own role.

migrate.name: Migrate VM
migrate.description: Live-migrate a VM to another online node. Use it before taking a node down for maintenance.

vmid.name: VM ID
vmid.description: The VM's numeric ID, for example 100.

target.name: Target node
target.description: The node name to move it to, for example pve2.
